                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:557" />6 But now <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 3.6.</ns0:note> hath he obtained a more excel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lent ministry <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>But,</ns0:hi> is here <ns0:hi>adversative</ns0:hi> setting this High-Priest over a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst and above the <ns0:hi>Aaronical,</ns0:hi> on the account both of his <ns0:hi>Ministry</ns0:hi> and Covenant, of which theirs were but Types and Shadows. The Lord Christ hath now really and fully ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained, and doth possess as the Gospel-High-Priest, a publick Ministration, which as to its glorious Effects, transcendently excels the Levitical, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.11, 12, 14. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 10.12, 14, 18.</ns0:note>, by how much also he is the Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diator <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>By how much</ns0:hi> he is Mediator of a better Covenant, <ns0:hi>by so much</ns0:hi> he hath a more excellent <ns0:hi>Ministry,</ns0:hi> so that this is a proof of the former. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> is a <ns0:hi>Midler,</ns0:hi> one that interposeth, not only between persons at <ns0:hi>distance,</ns0:hi> but at <ns0:hi>enmity</ns0:hi>; his par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lying between God and Sinners could profit little, God being so highly injured by, and offended with them; and therefore he <ns0:hi>mediates</ns0:hi> here as a <ns0:hi>Surety,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.22. and so undertakes for Sinners to satisfie God, wronged by them, by sacrificing him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self for them, and so secure the performance of his Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant-mercy to them. By which Sacrifice he purchaseth and merits the Holy Spirit, to enable Man to perform the Condi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions which God requireth from him, to repent, and believe, and obey the Redeemer, and wholly to rely upon his Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice for God's Favour; as by his <ns0:hi>Intercession</ns0:hi> he secures to them all the Blessings of God's Covenant for Time and Eternity, as proved, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.</ns0:note> of a better <ns0:note place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Testament.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> covenant <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The Gospel-Covenant,</ns0:hi> which was a solemn Agreement between an offended God and Sinners, wherein he binds himself to give forth Pardon and Life to them upon certain Conditions; and they bind themselves to per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />form, in order to the obtaining these. Which Covenant was brought about by the Intercession of Christ the <ns0:hi>Mediator</ns0:hi> be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tween them, who became a Surety for the performance of it, and solemnly ratified and confirmed it by the Sacrifice of himself; as other Covenants were by the Blood of federal Sacrifices, of which we have frequent mention in the Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, called <ns0:hi>better</ns0:hi> than the Mosaical Covenant, not for the matter of it, but for the manner of Exhibition, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.22. being comparatively a greater Good than that which was less, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.17.</ns0:note>, which was established upon better promises <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Which Gospel-Covenant was <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, as the Mosaical one, <ns0:hi>confirmed, ratified,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>established</ns0:hi> by the Blood of the Sacrifice according to the <ns0:hi>Law, ch.</ns0:hi> 9.18, to 21. This was its Sanction, it was by it setled un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />changeable, attended with, and founded on the <ns0:hi>best Promises,</ns0:hi> such as were more spiritual, clear, extensive and universall than those in the Mosaical Covenant were.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 For if that first <ns0:hi>covenant</ns0:hi> had been faultless <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This proves the Gospel-Covenant better than the Mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />saical; for if it had not, there would have been no second. That first Covenant, of which <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> was the Mediator, as to its Administration of it (as to the matter of it, it was the same from <ns0:hi>Adam</ns0:hi> throughout all Ages) was <ns0:hi>faulty,</ns0:hi> not because God made it, tho it was a less perfect Good, than what succeeded it. It was able to save those who would rightly use it, and come unto Christ by it, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.24. but <ns0:hi>accidentally</ns0:hi> by rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son of the Priests Faults, and Peoples sinfulness, it became wholly ineffectual to them for saving them, therefore the <ns0:hi>blame</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>fault</ns0:hi> of it is charged on them, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 8.</ns0:note>, then should no place have been sought for the second <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The Question here is vehemently assertive, <ns0:hi>if</ns0:hi> that Covenant in its Mosaical Administration had reached effectually its end, brought all that were under it to Christ, to be saved by him, no <ns0:hi>place,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:hi>room</ns0:hi> was there, that then being so perfect for another to succeed it, God would have rested there; but his excellent Wisdom and Counsel determined to put in being the <ns0:hi>second,</ns0:hi> and to set in the place of the <ns0:hi>first</ns0:hi> that was <ns0:hi>faulty,</ns0:hi> and which was to be abrogated by it, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.21.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For finding fault with them <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">This is the Proof of the faultiness of the Mosaical Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant, from the right cause of it, those who did abuse it. For <ns0:hi>Moses, Ioshua, Samuel, David,</ns0:hi> were saved by the right use of it. It did not bind them <ns0:hi>by Works</ns0:hi> to obtain <ns0:hi>Iustifica<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion,</ns0:hi> for it was delivered with <ns0:hi>Blood,</ns0:hi> which taught them it was to be had only <ns0:hi>by Faith in Christ</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Blood.</ns0:hi> But when they would not be led to Christ by it, they were <ns0:hi>faulty,</ns0:hi> and not the Covenant, and so they perished in their Gainsaying.                      <ns0:hi>Behold,</ns0:hi> imports Attention to, and Observation of the rare, excellent, and important thing proposed in the Word to the Eye and Mind of those for whom it was written, and to whom it is sent: so is this here in <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> 31.31. <ns0:hi>The days of the Messiah's coming</ns0:hi> in the Flesh, when a Woman shall compass a Man, as <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.22. the known times of Grace, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.5, 6.                      <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> A <ns0:hi>Covenant</ns0:hi> for form and manner of Administration <ns0:hi>second, later, better,</ns0:hi> stronger, and more excellent than the Mosaical; such as should be effectual to God's saving Ends in the Ministry of Christ, with the whole Seed of <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> the visible Church of God, when the Prophet wrote this, divided into two Kingdoms of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and that of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> removed a far off by the <ns0:hi>Assyrian,</ns0:hi> and seemingly lost, but by this Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant to be made one People again, and to be saved by <ns0:hi>Christ-David</ns0:hi> their King, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 23.5, 6. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 37.21, to 28.</ns0:note> a new covenant with the house of Israel, and the house of Judah:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The Spirit proceedeth to shew the Form of the Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant denied, not the same Covenant for habit or form, nor any like unto the same for the manner of its Administration, as was made by the Lord with the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> their Progenitors, when they were Strangers in <ns0:hi>Egypt,</ns0:hi> and under great Bon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dage there.</ns0:note>, in the day when I took them by the hand <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The day that I <ns0:hi>laid my Hand on them,</ns0:hi> and took hold of theirs, even the last day of the 430 years fore-told to <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> Gen. 15.13, 16. comp. <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 12.40, 41.
